'''Abe Sklar''' (November 25, 1925 – October 30, 2020) was an American mathematician and a professor of applied mathematics at the [[Illinois Institute of Technology]] (Illinois Tech) and the inventor of [[Copula (probability theory)|copulas]] in [[probability theory]].<ref>[https://science.iit.edu/people/faculty/abe-sklar Abe Sklar] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190502180215/https://science.iit.edu/people/faculty/abe-sklar |date=2019-05-02 }}, IIT College of Science, retrieved 2019-05-03.</ref>

== Education and career ==
Sklar was born in [[Chicago]] to Jewish parents who immigrated to the United States from [[Ukraine]]. He attended [[Von Steuben High School]] and later enrolled at the [[University of Chicago]] in 1942, when he was only 16. Sklar went on to become a student of [[Tom M. Apostol]] at the [[California Institute of Technology]], where he earned his Ph.D. in 1956. His students at IIT have included geometers [[Clark Kimberling]] and [[Marjorie Senechal]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=1313}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Genest |first=Christian |date=2021-01-01 |title=A tribute to Abe Sklar |journal=Dependence Modeling |language=en |volume=9 |issue=1 |pages=200–224 |doi=10.1515/demo-2021-0110 |issn=2300-2298|doi-access=free }}</ref>

In 1959, Sklar introduced the notion of and the name of "[[Copula (probability theory)|copulas]]" into [[probability theory]] and proved the theorem that bears his name, [[Copula (probability theory)#Sklar's theorem|Sklar's theorem]].<ref>[[Fabrizio Durante]] and [[Carlo Sempi]] (2016) Principles of Copula Theory, CRC Press, pp. ix</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Größer |first1=Joshua |last2=Okhrin |first2=Ostap |date=2022 |title=Copulae: An overview and recent developments |journal=WIREs Computational Statistics |language=en |volume=14 |issue=3 |article-number=e1557 |doi=10.1002/wics.1557 |issn=1939-5108|doi-access=free }}</ref>  That is, that [[cumulative distribution function#Multivariate case|multivariate cumulative distribution functions]] can be expressed in terms of copulas.<ref>{{citation | last=Sklar | first=A. | title=Fonctions de répartition à n dimensions et leurs marges | language=French | journal=Publ. Inst. Statist. Univ. Paris | year=1959 | volume=8 | pages=229–231}}.</ref> This representation of distribution functions, which is valid in any dimension and unique when the margins are continuous, is the basis of [[copula modeling]], a widespread data analytical technique used in statistics; this representation is often termed Sklar's representation. [[Construction of t-norms#Schweizer–Sklar t-norms|Schweizer–Sklar t-norms]] are also named after Sklar and Berthold Schweizer, who studied them together in the early 1960s.
